_documentation.purpose: Settings schema and category/section metadata owned by boost.
_documentation.consumer: extension/settings/controllers/ZentralSettingsCatalog.js reads schema/settings; Runtime filters availability, UI controllers render controls.

schema.label: Show the Boost widget
schema.description: On by default. Turn it off to hide the Boost-owned sidebar tile in the full pack or a standalone Boost install. On first start, a saved Sidebar Widgets Boost toggle is copied here only when this preference has no saved value; the old preference is left untouched.

schema.label: Free memory once after startup, when the browser has been quiet for 90 seconds
Unloading may include pinned and Essential tabs
schema.description: Off by default: they restore on demand like any tab, but they are your shortlist. Turn this on to let a deep pass include them. Renamed from keep_pinned in 3.4.0; an existing 'on' choice is carried over once.

schema.label: Keyboard shortcut for Free memory (light)
schema.description: For example Accel+Shift+B. Empty means no shortcut.

schema.label: Keep browser RAM under a limit
schema.description: Off by default. When on, Boost watches the total and acts only when it crosses the limit below.

schema.label: RAM limit (MB, total for all browser processes)
schema.description: The number the limiter compares the measured total against.

schema.label: What happens at the limit
schema.description: Soft only tells you; hard unloads tabs and panels the tab policy allows, three at a time, until the target is met.

options.label: Hard — unload what the policy allows

schema.label: Wait between limiter actions (seconds)
schema.description: A hard run never starts again inside this window, whatever the reading says.

schema.label: Stop a hard run at this share of the limit (%)
schema.description: The limiter stops unloading once the total falls to this percentage of the limit.

schema.label: Game Mode: pause everything else while I play
schema.description: Level 3 of Memory Boost. Runs ONE plan-driven unload pass through the panel sleep door, then a light clean after the settle and one late clean about 30 s later. Pauses repeating timers (widgets, video discovery, RSS, Notes) and stops painting tabs you are not looking at. Audible tabs, the video preview source, sharing/PiP/private/add-on host tabs and configured keep-hosts stay loaded. Unloaded tabs lose unsaved page state and need a short reload when you return; Restore is available. Off when the browser restarts.

schema.label: Stronger saver: also sleep apps marked 'keep running'
schema.description: Off by default. OUTSIDE Game Mode, this opens every Essential-panel background mode (including live/keep running) to a manual Level 2 deep pass. Game Mode does not depend on it; a plain deep pass still sleeps only asleep-allowed records.

schema.label: Game Mode: sites that must stay loaded (host names, comma-separated)
schema.description: Optional. A tab whose host matches one of these names is kept, for example music.example.com, bank.example.com. Empty keeps nothing extra.

schema.label: Game Mode: park the selected tab so it can be unloaded too
schema.description: On by default. Game Mode creates one temporary about:blank parking tab, selects it from a deferred task, then unloads the original. Turn this off to keep the old behavior where the selected tab always stays loaded.

schema.label: Game Mode: what Restore brings back
schema.description: All tabs, the most recent tabs, panels only, or nothing. Panels are woken first; tabs reload in the background without changing selection. Unloaded pages lose unsaved form state and need a short reload.

schema.label: Game Mode: number of recent tabs to restore
schema.description: Used by the recent profile. Newest last-accessed tabs come first; zero restores no tabs.

schema.label: Game Mode: delay between restore items (ms)
schema.description: One item starts per one-shot timer, at most two loading at once. Zero is allowed but restores everything as fast as the browser answers.

schema.label: Game Mode: Restore when the mode is switched off
schema.description: Ask shows the Restore action; always runs Restore automatically; never leaves the snapshot for a manual Restore. This is the kill switch for automatic restore on exit.
